sections.skill: Explain how AI, machine learning and deep learning nest

questions.domain: Foundation 1: What AI is and where it appears
questions.prompt: How are AI, machine learning and deep learning related?

choices.text: They are three different words for exactly the same thing
AI is part of deep learning, which is part of machine learning
Deep learning is part of machine learning, which is part of AI
Machine learning and deep learning are unrelated to AI

questions.correct_answer: Deep learning is part of machine learning, which is part of AI
questions.intro: MACHINE LEARNING is a way of building AI in which a system improves at a task by learning patterns from data instead of following only hand-written rules. DEEP LEARNING is one kind of machine learning. It uses NEURAL NETWORKS: many connected layers of simple math units. Each layer passes numbers to the next, and early layers pick up simple features while later layers combine them into more complex ones. "Deep" means many layers, not deep understanding. So the ideas nest like boxes: deep learning sits inside machine learning, which sits inside AI. Not all AI uses machine learning, and not all machine learning is deep learning.
questions.feedback: The groups nest: deep learning inside machine learning inside AI.

questions.intro: Picture three boxes that fit inside each other. The biggest box is labeled ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE: any computer system doing thinking-like tasks. Inside it sits a smaller box, MACHINE LEARNING: AI that learns patterns from data. Inside that sits the smallest box, DEEP LEARNING: machine learning that uses neural networks with many layers. Everything in a small box is also in the boxes around it, but the big box holds other things too. A chess program built only from hand-written rules sits in the AI box but outside the machine learning box.

sections.title: Apply it

sections.skill: Read claims about neural networks and deep learning carefully

questions.domain: Foundation 1: What AI is and where it appears
questions.prompt: An ad says its "neural network works just like a human brain." What is the problem with this claim?

choices.text: Neural networks cannot be used in any products
Neural networks are math inspired by a biology word, not brains
Neural networks are physically built from brain cells
Nothing; that comparison is scientifically exact

questions.correct_answer: Neural networks are math inspired by a biology word, not brains
questions.intro: People often use these terms loosely, so read claims carefully. "Neural network" borrows a word from biology, but these networks are math, not brains: the comparison helped early researchers and can mislead beginners. "Deep" counts layers; it does not mean wise or thoughtful. Deep learning often needs much more data and computing power than simpler machine learning, and simpler methods can work as well on small, tidy problems such as predicting sales from a few numbers. Choosing an approach depends on the task, the data available and the need to explain results.
questions.feedback: The brain comparison is a loose analogy.
